text: Stars serve as the foundation for astronomy, yet they never remain fixed; instead, they orbit a universal center. A star's path depends entirely on its separation from that center and its velocity. Meteorite impacts on our planet shatter rocks and strip away the crust to create craters. Among these depressions, the spherical variety is most prevalent, resulting from high-speed strikes by large bodies such as comets or asteroids. Consequently, evidence of these frequent collisions appears both across Earth's terrain and on the lunar surface.
